title: Anatomy: how a board becomes a map
goal: Understand how a board your agent writes into the repository becomes a map you can explore and mark up, and how your marks go back to the agent and come back answered.

includes: Opening a repository folder or a file, checking the board, and showing it as a map
Your layer: notes, links, drawings, proposed parts, and moved connections, with undo
Send to agent and the answers that come back in the next revision
excludes: How the agent decides what to write: the app only reads the board
How the map routes lines and places labels in detail

components.label: Your agent
components.summary: Any coding agent you already use. It writes the board, and later reads your feedback and answers it in a new revision.
components.explanation: Anatomy has no built-in AI and makes no network calls. Your agent works in the repository as it always does. `.anatomy/README.md`, which Anatomy writes, tells it the board format and how to answer feedback.
inputs: What you ask it to explain

components.label: Board file
components.summary: The agent's explanation in .anatomy/board.json: parts, connections, open questions, walkthroughs, and answers to your feedback.
components.explanation: Each part and connection says where the claim comes from. A new revision has a higher `revision` number and keeps the IDs of what stayed, so your notes stay attached. Commit it with the code it explains.

components.label: Feedback file
components.summary: What you send to the agent, in .anatomy/feedback.json. Every mark is described by what it means on the board, never in pixels.
components.explanation: A drawing becomes the parts it encloses and the lines it touches. A moved connection becomes its old and new ends. Each item has an ID, and the agent answers each one by that ID.
inputs: Your marks, from Send to agent
outputs: Items for the agent to answer

components.label: Layer file
components.summary: Your own layer, saved in .anatomy/layer.json a moment after each change. Other browsers keep it in this browser instead.
components.explanation: It is kept apart from the board, so a new revision never overwrites your work. It holds only the cards you moved, so new parts still follow the layout. Keep it out of version control.
outputs: Your layer when you open the folder again

components.label: Workspace
components.summary: Opens the repository folder in Chrome or Edge, or a single file elsewhere. It watches the board file and opens each new revision.
components.explanation: The folder is remembered, so the next visit asks only for permission again. The board file is checked every two seconds while the tab is visible, and read once it stops changing.
inputs: Your choice of folder or file

components.label: Validator
components.summary: Checks the size, format, fields, and IDs of a board, and that every connection points at a real part.
components.explanation: A board is data only. Nothing in it is run, fetched, or shown as HTML. A broken file is rejected with a list of what is wrong, and the open board stays.

components.label: App state
components.summary: One store that holds the open board, your layer, the selection, and the history for undo and redo.
components.explanation: Every change to your layer is one step of undo. A new revision and a send are barriers that undo does not cross. When a revision arrives, the answers in it are put next to your items.

components.label: Map
components.summary: Draws each part as a card and each connection as a line that routes around the cards. You can drag, resize, pan, and zoom.
components.explanation: Cards are laid out as a flow from the connections. A card you move keeps its place, and a drop pushes overlapped cards aside.

components.label: Whiteboard
components.summary: Tools to mark up the map: pen, rectangle, ellipse, arrow, text, sticky note, and new part. You can also drag the end of a connection to another part.
components.explanation: Everything you make is drawn in your color, apart from the agent's content. A moved connection shows your new line, with the original dimmed until the agent answers.
outputs: Marks, new parts, and moved ends

components.label: Sidebar
components.summary: Shows the board overview or the selection: what flows in and out of a part, its explanation, open items, notes, and the agent's answers.
components.explanation: The Review tab appears after a new revision. It lists answers, notes that need a look, and what changed, including moved connections with their old and new ends.

components.label: Command menu
components.summary: Every action in one searchable list, with its shortcut. It also finds parts and connections by name.
components.explanation: Buttons, tooltips, and keys all read the same list, so a shortcut shown anywhere is the one that works.

components.label: Your layer
components.summary: Everything you add on top of the board: positions, sizes, notes, links, drawings, proposed parts, and moved connections.
components.explanation: Items the agent adopted move to an archive once the board shows the change. Declined and answered items keep their answer until you dismiss them. Nothing is deleted on its own, and the archive can be restored.

components.label: Send to agent
components.summary: Writes your new and changed items to the feedback file and copies a short prompt that you paste to your agent.
components.explanation: It shows what will go first, and lists drawings that say nothing so you can fix them. Items with no answer yet go again with the next send, so a second send never drops them.

components.label: Review
components.summary: Compares a new revision with the one you had, and shows the agent's answers next to your items.
components.explanation: Each part and connection has a fingerprint. A note whose part changed is marked possibly outdated, and a note whose part left the board asks to be attached again.

relationships.label: writes a revision
relationships.explanation: The agent writes the whole board as one file and saves a new revision each time it changes it. Everything you see on the map starts from this file.

relationships.label: each revision
relationships.explanation: The workspace watches the board file. When a new revision is saved, it reads the text and hands it on, so you never reload by hand.

relationships.label: file text
relationships.explanation: The raw text of the file goes to the validator, which checks it before anything is shown. A file that fails the check never reaches the map.

relationships.label: checked board
relationships.explanation: Only a board that passed the check is stored. The map and the sidebar then read from this one copy and cannot show a broken board.

relationships.label: cards and lines
relationships.explanation: The map receives the board and your layer and turns them into cards and lines. When the store changes, the map redraws.

relationships.label: clicks and drops
relationships.explanation: When you click, drag, or drop on the map, the map tells the store what you did. The store keeps the selection and the undo history, not the map.

relationships.label: selection
relationships.explanation: The sidebar shows whatever you have selected, so it reads the selection from the store. Pick a part and its details appear.

relationships.label: commands
relationships.explanation: Each command you run from the menu becomes the same change as clicking the matching button. The menu holds no state of its own.

relationships.label: marks and moved ends
relationships.explanation: Every drawing, sticky note, proposed part, and moved connection end is saved in your layer. Your marks stay apart from the agent's board.

relationships.label: notes and links
relationships.explanation: Notes and links you write in the sidebar go into your layer, attached to a part or a connection by its ID.

relationships.label: saves
relationships.explanation: A moment after each change, your layer is written to its file. That keeps your positions and notes when you close the tab.

relationships.label: your items
relationships.explanation: Send to agent collects the items you added or changed from your layer. It leaves out anything you have not touched.

relationships.label: writes
relationships.explanation: Each item is described by what it means on the board, such as "a question about this part", and written to the feedback file. It never records pixel positions.

relationships.label: reads
relationships.explanation: The agent reads the feedback file to learn what you asked, then answers each item in the next revision of the board.

relationships.label: new revision
relationships.explanation: When a new revision arrives, the store starts the Review. It compares the new board with the one you had.

relationships.label: answers and archive
relationships.explanation: The agent's answers are placed next to the items they answer. Items that are settled move to an archive so your layer stays short.

items.text: The app checks the shape of a board, not whether its content is true. Source labels tell you how much to trust each part.
Opening a folder needs Chrome or Edge. Other browsers open a board file and download the feedback file instead.
Whether the agent answers every item depends on the agent. An item with no answer goes again with the next send.
Should Anatomy add layer.json and feedback.json to .gitignore itself, or only recommend it?

steps.caption: Your agent writes .anatomy/board.json in the repository.
You open the repository folder, and the workspace reads the board file.
The validator checks every field and ID before anything is shown.
The checked board goes into the app state, and the map lays out the cards.
You click a card, and the sidebar explains it.

scenarios.title: Mark it up and send it to the agent

steps.caption: You circle two parts, ask a question, and drag a connection to another part. Each change is one step of undo.
Your layer is saved to .anatomy/layer.json a moment later.
Send to agent shows what will go, then writes the feedback file and copies a prompt.
You paste the prompt, and your agent reads the feedback file.

scenarios.title: The agent answers in a new revision

steps.caption: The agent writes the next revision with an answer to every item, and moves the connection you dragged.
The workspace notices the new file and opens it once it stops changing.
The answers go next to your items. The moved connection was adopted, so your line moves to the archive and the agent's line shows.
The Review tab shows the answers and what changed. You dismiss what you read, and can restore anything from the archive.
The agent writes a board with a connection that points at a part that does not exist.
The validator lists the problem and stops. The board that was already open stays on screen.
